nodes.dialogText: You approach a woman in an oil stained shirt peering into the lifted hood of a truck. Another car is parked in the driveway as well.
You the one talking about fire safety?

options.messageText: Yes I am. I would love to help if I can.
That's a pretty nice truck you got there. Same with the car.

nodes.dialogText: Appreciate it. Rebuilt both of them myself.
The name's Bailey, by the way.
So, think you can advise me, or what?

options.messageText: It's nice to meet you Bailey. What can I do to help?

nodes.dialogText: Glad to see someone helping out around here. My name's Bailey.

options.messageText: It's nice to meet you Bailey. What can I do to help?

nodes.dialogText: Well, everyone's been buzzing about wildfire safety. So my partner and I've been thinking about it too.
We got two jobs and these two cars, so making a plan is tricky.

options.messageText: Having two cars could help. What's your plan if a fire gets close?
Have you thought about how two cars might make evacuating harder?

nodes.dialogText: Yeah, we've been debating that.
Having one car is simpler, and faster.
It would reduce the traffic on the road, which would help everyone.
But two cars means more options. Plus. I'd be hard to leave one car behind, since it's so valuable to us.

options.messageText: Have you considered relocating the second car to somewhere safer beforehand?

nodes.dialogText: We was thinking about driving both, so we could pack more and save both vehicles.
But, traffic is what concerns me. I don't want one us getting caught up.

options.messageText: It makes sense to not want to be seperated, or risk someone getting hurt because they were stuck in traffic.
Have you considered relocating the second car to somewhere safer beforehand?

nodes.dialogText: Have you thought about just taking one car?
Yeah, we've thought about that too.
Having one car is simpler, and faster.
But two cars means more options. Plus. I'd be hard to leave one car behind, since it's so valuable to us.
Hm, I think that could work. I know a garage we could stash one of the cars at.
It would take some planning ahead though, which could be timely.
What is best for Bailey?

You see a man attempting to gather a mountain of childrens toys in his arms. Upon seeing you, he unsuccessfully piles the toys in the front yard, with several balls escaping and rolling into the grass.
One soccer ball bumps past you as he approaches to give you a handshake.
Hey there friend! My name's Gabe. It's great to chat with ya.
You actually caught me at a pretty good time. The kids are at after school soccer practice, so I don't have to wrangle them in right now.

options.messageText: It's nice to meet you Gabe. Seems like you got some pretty sporty kids!
It's nice to meet you Gabe. What seems to be the problem?

nodes.dialogText: You're tellin me! My partner Sam and I have had turn our garage basically into a sporting goods store just to store all their team equipment!
My two kiddos are elementary age, so they play pretty much every sport you can think of. We're always on the road for another game.

options.messageText: What advice can I offer to help you?

nodes.dialogText: Well, with wildfire season coming up, my partner Sam and I have been trying to plan in case of emergency.
We've got two young kids, elementary school age. We're not sure what to do if a fire hits while they're at school.

options.messageText: Have you talked to the school about their wildfire evacuation plans?

nodes.dialogText: The school has a plan, but I can't help but feel uneasy.
Being apart from your kids during an evacuation is scary - I would much prefer it if we were together.

options.messageText: Being worried about being seperated is completely understandable.
Being worried about being seperated is completely understandable.

nodes.dialogText: Schools are safer during a wildfire - it might help to trust the school's plan so you can focus on your own evacuation.
That way you're ready to go get your kids the second you are contacted to!
That's true, I do trust the school to have a solid plan in case of emergency.
As a parent, it's just so tough to leave them

options.messageText: Being worried about being seperated is completely understandable.
It might ease your anxiety to reach out to the school again. They could host a conference or meeting discussing these topics.

nodes.dialogText: Are you considering picking them up to be safe?
We have been thinking about it, but another concern is traffic.
I want to pick them up, but the roads could be jammed.

options.messageText: Maybe you could coordinate with other parents to carpool, or ensure everyone is safe?
Have you thought about picking them up early out of school? That might help with the traffic concerns.

nodes.dialogText: That isn't a bad idea at all. It would take some planning, but that way we at least know our children are alright.
There still is always the issue of traffic, even with a carpool.
We have, and it isn't a bad idea. That might get us ahead of most of the traffic, but we also need to consider our commute from our jobs to the school.
That would be the perfect place to present your concerns, and make sure they are addressed!
That isn't a bad idea at all. If I had a better understanding of their plan, I know Sam and I would feel a lot safer about our kids.
What is best for Gabe and Sam?
A woman is turned away from you on a stepladder, painting the side of her home. She looks in your direction, and waves. She climbs down the ladder and approaches you, wiping sweat off her brow.
Hey there! I'm Sarah, it's nice to meet you. My husband Jerry is busy right now, but I can catch him up later.
I do hope you can help us out.
I'm just finishing up painting the exterior of our house!
We bought this house as a fixer-upper. A year and a lot of money later, we are putting in the final touches.
It's the main reason why I called you here, actually.
Living in the wildland-urban interface is incredibly stressful during fire season.
We've invested so much fixing up this house; it was a fixer upper and we're just now starting to see results. It's hard to decide the best next plan.
What do you think are some options?

options.messageText: Home hardening is the process of making your home more resistant to wildfires. That can be a good option, especially living in a WUI.
An early evacuation, especially on Red Flag days, can be the world's difference to your safety. With the traffic, commotion, and panic, it never hurts to get out early.

nodes.dialogText: Some examples of home hardening are choosing fire resistant materials, clearing debris, and clearly marking your address on the street for emergency responders.
That makes a lot of sense, it could save money in the long run investing in home hardening.
However, money is tight, so I would have to cut costs in other parts of my life first.

options.messageText: An early evacuation, especially on Red Flag days, can be the world's difference to your safety. With the traffic, commotion, and panic, it never hurts to get out early.

nodes.dialogText: That also makes sense. At the end of the day, safety should be the number one priority.
The only problem is, there are so many Red Flag days, it would be stressful to evacuate every single time. That's too much.

options.messageText: What do you think about those options?

nodes.dialogText: That makes sense. At the end of the day, safety should be the number one priority.
The only problem is, there are so many Red Flag days, it would be stressful to evacuate every single time. That's too much.

options.messageText: Home hardening is the process of making your home more resistant to wildfires. That can also be a good option, especially living in a WUI.

nodes.dialogText: Some examples of home hardening are choosing fire resistant materials, clearing debris, and clearly marking your address on the street for emergency responders.
That makes a lot of sense, it could save money in the long run investing in home hardening.
However, money is tight, so I would have to cut costs in other parts of my life first.

options.messageText: What do you think about those options?

nodes.dialogText: It's definitely a lot to think about.
Home hardening is a great way to protect your home in a wildfire. We've worked so hard on this place, I want to do everything I can to keep it safe.
But at the end of the day, our lives are more important. We can rebuild, like we did when we bought this home. Early evacuations can ensure that my husband Jerry and I are safe.
Both require time, and resources, each of which are limited. I'll do my best to do both, but I need to decide one to prefer.
What do you think?

Hello dear, it’s nice you’re checking in. I’ve lived here for decades, but with wildfires getting worse, I get nervous every season. It’s harder for me to move quickly, so I need to be extra prepared. Any advice?

options.optionText: Planning for an early evacuation is important. Have you thought about leaving early when there’s a red flag warning?
Do you have neighbors or family who can help you if you need to evacuate quickly?

nodes.dialogText: I’ve have, but it’s tough to leave before anyone else. It feels like I’m abandoning my home. What if it's a false alarm?

options.optionText: I understand, but leaving early ensures your safety. Fires move faster than we expect.
You’re not abandoning your home—you’re giving yourself the best chance to stay safe.

nodes.dialogText: I have a few kind neighbors who could help, but I hate to be a burden. And my kids live hours away, so it’s hard for them to help in an emergency.

options.optionText: It’s good to have supportive neighbors. Can you make a plan together so no one feels overwhelmed?
What about organizing a checklist for what you’d need to take? So you are more prepared.

nodes.dialogText: It's a lot to think about, I hope I make the best choice.

You see a person playing fetch with two large dogs. As you approach, the two dogs bound over, dropping a slobbery ball at your feet. Their owner jogs over, and waves hello, before picking up the ball and tossing it, the dogs not far behind.
Pippin, Porkchop, fetch!
Those dogs are tireless! I feel like I could charge a battery off of them.
They wipe slobber off their pants before extending for a handshake.
My name's Genaro. I appreciate you stopping by!

options.messageText: Pleasure to meet you Genaro. How can I help?
Those are some really cute dogs. Do you have other pets?

nodes.dialogText: Yeah I do! I'm the proud parent of two dogs, a cat, and two rabbits.
I'm a notorious foster failure. Sometimes they're just too cute! I can't help it they would leave a pet sized hole in my heart if I let them go.
They're actually the reason I called you here.
Wildfire season stresses me out. Like really stresses me out.
But not because of me. Because of my pets!
I've got two dogs, a cat, and two rabbits, all of whom I love with my entire heart.
If the fire gets close, I need a plan to get everyone to safety.

options.messageText: A detailed evacuation plan, with supplies and transport ready, can help when it's time to leave.
Evacuating with pets is tricky, maybe pre-evacuating with them on red flag days could help?

nodes.dialogText: I've got crates and carriers for all of them, but getting them out quickly is tough.
Rabbits are incredibly skittish - if they hide, it would take forever to try and find them fast!

options.messageText: Doing a practice run might help you prepare before an actual emergency.
Having a go-bag ready for each pet - food, water, medicine - makes a huge difference in a rush.
Evacuating with pets is tricky, maybe pre-evacuating with them on red flag days could help?

nodes.dialogText: Definetly. I've been trying to keep a go bag ready.
The only issue is that some items expire after a period of time. It's costly to upkeep a go bag.

options.messageText: Doing a practice run might help you prepare before an actual emergency.
Evacuating with pets is tricky, maybe pre-evacuating with them on red flag days could help?

nodes.dialogText: It would be a great way to catch things you might have previously overlooked.
Oh you're so right! There are absolutely some things I have overlooked, it wouldn't hurt at all to practice.
It might also help with my bunny wrangling skills.
I've thought about it, but it feels extreme to leave before an order.
Plus, where would we go? Finding a pet-friendly place is tough.

options.messageText: Some shelters or hotels allow pets, and leaving early can help you avoid last-minute panic.
If you have family or friends in a safer area, maybe you could stay with them when it's risky?

nodes.dialogText: That isn't a bad idea. I would have to do a lot of research.
I worry that a lot of those places will fill up quick. What would I do then if they were full?

options.messageText: If you have family or friends in a safer area, maybe you could stay with them when it's risky?
A detailed evacuation plan, with supplies and transport ready, can help when it's time to leave.

nodes.dialogText: That's not a bad idea. I would just hate to be a burden though.
I'm used to taking care of this many animals, but I understand why a lot of others wouldn't.
I also know it would stress my pets out a lot! I don't want to overwhelm them by evacuating too much.

options.messageText: Some shelters or hotels allow pets, and leaving early can help you avoid last-minute panic.
A detailed evacuation plan, with supplies and transport ready, can help when it's time to leave.

nodes.dialogText: What is best for Genaro?
Hey there! Thank you for coming into town to help our community learn about fire awareness. You can Click or Tap to read the next message.
Before we start, would you like to review your job? Or are you ready to get started?

options.messageText: I think a review of my tasks would be great!
I think I'm ready now.

nodes.dialogText: Fantastic! Let's get started. As firefighters, our job is to help our neighbors be fire safe.
Not just when fires start, but beforehand as well.

When people prepare ahead of time for wildfires, they can keep their homes and families much safer. They have a lot more time to make important decisions, such as home hardening, what to pack, and evacuation procedures.

Unfortunately, a lot of people struggle to create a plan. It’s hard to know what’s best for your situation...
...which is where you come in!

options.messageText: How can I help with people's wildfire plans?

nodes.dialogText: You will be speaking to members of our community, and helping them make their plan!
Earlier, I got a call from Mary, a neighbor of ours. Let's go speak to her, and see if we can help!

options.messageText: Let's go!

nodes.dialogText: Oh good! Thank you so much for coming. Fire season is close, and I’m a little worried.

options.messageText: What's worrying you about this fire season?
Hi Mary, I'm happy to help you.

nodes.dialogText: Well, I’ve recently started fostering animals! I have two dogs, and the cutest litter of kittens!

options.messageText: Are you concerned about keeping your pets safe?

nodes.dialogText: Thank you! But now I start to worry about what to do if a fire starts. There’s so many supplies for them, and I’m afraid I’ll be panicking and scrambled!
Exactly. I’m worried about what to do if a fire starts. There’s so many supplies for them, and I’m afraid I’ll be panicking and scrambled!
Everyone will have a different situation, and different concerns. It’s important to listen, and respond accordingly!
In this case, the best way to keep pets safe is to include them in the family plan. A great step is to keep extra pet supplies packed in a go bag.
How about you tell Mary, then we’ll head out.

options.messageText: You should prepare your pets supplies as you would with your own! Creating a go bag full of their necessary supplies, along with animal crates, is a great way to stay ready, and ensure you and your pets can leave at a moments notice!

nodes.dialogText: That’s a great idea, I’ll try to get that done! It’s hard to stay on top of things, but I know it will be relieving in the long run.

options.messageText: Happy to help!

nodes.dialogText: You can see you spoke to Mary from the . Great work! Now, you can see all the other homes that need your help.
Once you have spoken to everyone, press on that icon. Then we will see what happened, and the impact you made!

options.messageText: Sounds good! I think I'm ready now.

nodes.dialogText: Great! Oh, one last thing.
Sometimes, even with advice, people might not listen. This could be from a bunch of different reasons, but it’s important to keep in mind that their actions might not reflect what you told them.
Just listen to each situation, and do what you think is best! Are you ready to begin?

options.messageText: Yes
